prompt: Build a tiny generational genetic algorithm that tracks the best fitness ever seen as well as the best one currently alive. Complete the EvolutionTracker class in the starter file.
explanation: Without elitism nothing protects the current champion, so the best fitness in a population can fall from one generation to the next -- which is exactly why a separate best-ever field is worth keeping. The class is a state machine over a population array: each step selects two parents per child by tournament, mixes them gene by gene, mutates, and only afterwards swaps the new population in. The strict order of random draws matters as much as the logic, because selection then crossover then mutation, all from one Random, is what lets a run replay identically from its seed.
hints: Build the entire next generation into a new int[size][geneLength] before assigning it to the population field -- mutating in place would let later children breed from earlier children.
Crossover and mutation are two separate loops over the genes, in that order, so the number of draws per child is always 2 + 2 * geneLength.
bestEver is only ever raised, never lowered: compare it with bestFitness() at the end of step and keep the larger.
